## [BUG] items

### [BUG] Engine — 17 overlays are never hidden by any reset path

**Where:** `js/engine.js` — `resetToLobby()` (and the per-game reset functions it delegates to: `resetSyllySignals`, `resetSecretMode`, `resetYouGetIt`, `resetLateToTheParty`, `natResetState`, `dsdResetState`, `bldResetState`, `gthResetState`)
**What:** These overlays are hidden only by their own close/cancel buttons — no reset path touches them: `settings-overlay`, `deck-panel`, `skip-turn-overlay` (LI5); `gm-settings-overlay`, `gm-near-sync-overlay`, `gm-boost-overlay`, `gm-neural-library-overlay`, `gm-new-frequency-overlay`, `gm-vocab-overlay`, `gm-concede-overlay`, `gm-deck-panel`, `gm-how-to-overlay` (GM); `ss-settings-overlay`, `ss-dossier-overlay`, `ss-how-to-overlay` (SS); `lttp-smalltalk-overlay` (LTTP); `sound-overlay` (global). Verified by scripted token-exact sweep of `resetToLobby()` + all delegated reset bodies (13 June 2026).
**Why it matters:** In Lobby Mode, `resetToLobby()` can fire while any overlay is open (host taps end-game, or client confirms the host-disconnected overlay) — the stale overlay then survives on top of the lobby, the DYB BUG-05 ghost-interceptor class. LI5, GM, SS, and LTTP are all multiplayer-capable, so every listed overlay is reachable in this window.
**Fix:** Add a `style.display = 'none'` for each listed overlay to `resetToLobby()` (or to the owning game's delegated reset function); `sound-overlay` can be added to the engine's own teardown block.
**Verify:** Re-run the sweep: every `fixed inset-0` overlay id in `index.html` appears (token-exact or via template-literal loop) in `resetToLobby()` + delegate bodies; manually open GM settings on a client device, kill the host, confirm OK → lobby shows with no stale overlay.
**Rule violated:** `phase-audit.md` Protocol C Part 2 (`resetToLobby()` teardown row); DYB BUG-05 lesson

### [BUG] BLD — lobby has no `getMinPlayers` at all; engine default allows a 2-player start (role table starts at 5)

**Where:** `js/engine-multiplayer.js` — `MP_GAME_CONFIGS.bld` (lines ~206–212) and the fallback `mpActiveGameConfig?.getMinPlayers?.() ?? 2` (line ~1471)
**What:** The BLD config defines `getMaxPlayers: () => 10` but no `getMinPlayers`, so the lobby falls back to the engine default of **2**. `BLD_ROLE_TABLE` and `BLD_GROUP_TABLE` in `bld.js` have no row below 5 (the game is designed for 5–10; `game-identities.md` documents min 5). (Phase 2 of this audit logged this as `getMinPlayers: () => 4` — that was a misread of GTH's neighbouring entry; reality is the field is absent entirely.)
**Why it matters:** A 2–4 player start looks up `BLD_ROLE_TABLE[count]` → `undefined`, crashing role assignment or silently producing a broken game for all devices.
**Fix:** Add `getMinPlayers: () => 5` to the BLD entry of `MP_GAME_CONFIGS`.
**Verify:** Host a BLD lobby with 4 joined players — the start CTA must stay disabled; with 5 it enables.
**Rule violated:** `game-identities.md` § Game 11 Bailed (Min players: 5)

### [BUG] PASS — `MP_GAME_CONFIGS.pass` missing display fields; mode screen renders "undefined"

**Where:** `js/engine-multiplayer.js` — `MP_GAME_CONFIGS.pass` (lines ~257–275) and `mpShowModeScreen()` (lines ~400–405)
**What:** The PASS config has a stray `gameId: 'pass'` key (read by nothing) and is missing the four display fields every other game defines: `gameName`, `emoji`, `ptpLabel`, `brandBtnClass`. `mpShowModeScreen()` unconditionally writes all four into the mode screen — and PASS's menu Play CTA does route through `mpShowModeScreen('pass')` (`pass.js` line ~1289).
**Why it matters:** Every PASS multiplayer entry shows a mode screen with "undefined" as the emoji, "undefined" as the game name, a CTA labelled "undefined", and a CTA `className` containing the literal string `undefined` (no background colour — white text on white).
**Fix:** Add `gameName: 'Pass'`, `emoji: '🃏'`, `ptpLabel: 'Deal Me In'`, `brandBtnClass: 'bg-zinc-900 hover:bg-zinc-800'` to the PASS entry and delete the stray `gameId` key.
**Verify:** Tap Pass → Deal Me In from the lobby: mode screen shows 🃏 / "Pass" and a black branded CTA reading "Deal Me In".
**Rule violated:** `ui-style.md` § Per-game brand reference (PASS row); `logic-engine.md` § Multiplayer checklist (MP_GAME_CONFIGS entry)

## [POLISH] items

### [POLISH] LTTP — orphaned `screen-lttp-smalltalk` section (dead markup)

**Where:** `index.html` — `<section id="screen-lttp-smalltalk">`
**What:** A full `<section>` for a Small Talk screen exists but is never referenced by `lttp.js`, never registered in `allScreens[]`, and never shown — it is a leftover from before the Phase 21a redesign that made Small Talk an overlay (`lttp-smalltalk-overlay`, which is the live element).
**Why it matters:** Dead markup in a single-file SPA misleads future sessions (it contains `lttp-st-*` IDs that look live) and bloats the file.
**Fix:** Delete the entire `screen-lttp-smalltalk` section via a Node script (index.html bulk-edit rule), after confirming none of its child IDs (`lttp-st-ask-*`) are referenced in `lttp.js`.
**Verify:** Grep `lttp.js` for each removed child ID → zero hits; Small Talk Helper still works via `lttp-smalltalk-overlay`.
**Rule violated:** `phase-audit.md` 2B-10 (orphaned markup)

### [POLISH] GTH — Play CTA contains an emoji

**Where:** `index.html` — `#btn-gth-menu-play` ("Start the Session 🛋️")
**What:** The game menu Play CTA includes an emoji, violating the rule "CTA start-game buttons (game menu) must not contain emoji" (`ui-style.md` § Settings Card Standard).
**Why it matters:** Cross-game inconsistency — all other 11 Play CTAs are text-only.
**Fix:** Remove the 🛋️ from the button label (one-off single-element edit — fine without a script).
**Verify:** Open GTH menu; CTA reads "Start the Session" with no emoji.
**Rule violated:** `ui-style.md` § Settings Card Standard (CTA emoji rule)

### [POLISH] DYB — how-to overlay uses muted stone-400 instead of brand stone-700

**Where:** `index.html` — `dyb-how-to-overlay`: step labels `text-stone-400`, close button `bg-stone-400 hover:bg-stone-500`
**What:** Step labels and the close button use stone-400, lighter than DYB's stone-700 brand; every other game uses its full brand colour for both.
**Why it matters:** Visual drift from the How-to Overlay Standard; the close button reads as disabled-grey.
**Fix:** If unintentional, change step labels to `text-stone-700` and close button to `bg-stone-700 hover:bg-stone-800` (Node script if batch-editing; individual edits fine). If a deliberate muted choice, document it in `ui-style.md`'s per-game table note instead.
**Verify:** DYB how-to overlay step labels and close button match the brand table row.
**Rule violated:** `ui-style.md` § How-to Overlay Standard

### [POLISH] GM / LTTP / NAT — doubled `id` attribute on the header `[?]` buttons

**Where:** `index.html` lines ~729 (`btn-gm-how-to`), ~3323 (`btn-lttp-how-to`), ~3889 (`btn-nat-how-to`)
**What:** Each of these three buttons has the same `id` attribute written twice on the one tag (`id="btn-gm-how-to" id="btn-gm-how-to"`). Browsers ignore the duplicate attribute, so behaviour is unaffected — there is no second element.
**Why it matters:** Invalid HTML; a future regex-based sweep (like this audit's) counts them as duplicate IDs and wastes investigation time.
**Fix:** Remove the second `id="..."` from each of the three tags (one-off single-element edits — fine without a script).
**Verify:** Scripted duplicate-id sweep over `index.html` reports zero duplicates.
**Rule violated:** — (markup hygiene)

### [POLISH] css/styles.css — dead `.pill.pill-active` rule (bare `pill-active` never referenced)

**Where:** `css/styles.css` lines ~48–51 — `.pill.pill-active { background: #ec4899; ... }`
**What:** The suffix-less `pill-active` class is defined (pink-500) but referenced nowhere in `index.html` or any JS file — every live usage is `pill-active-[colour]`.
**Why it matters:** Dead code invites accidental reuse; it predates the per-game colour family.
**Fix:** Delete the `.pill.pill-active` rule block.
**Verify:** Grep `index.html` + `js/` for `pill-active"` / `'pill-active'` (bare, no suffix) → zero hits; pill toggles still style correctly.
**Rule violated:** `phase-audit.md` Protocol A §2 (dead/deprecated class)

### [POLISH] index.html — Google Fonts loaded from CDN; brand font is network-dependent

**Where:** `index.html` `<head>` — `<link>` tags to `fonts.googleapis.com` / `fonts.gstatic.com` (Fredoka)
**What:** The Fredoka font is loaded from Google Fonts at runtime and is not (and cannot trivially be) precached by the SW; the project's documented constraint is "local Tailwind, no CDN, fully offline".
**Why it matters:** Offline/installed PWA sessions silently fall back to the system font — the app works but loses its brand typography, and the docs overstate the offline guarantee.
**Fix:** Either self-host Fredoka (download the woff2 files into e.g. `css/fonts/`, add a local `@font-face`, add to `sw.js` precache, bump SW) or document the deliberate exception in `CLAUDE.md` § Tech Stack and `logic-engine.md` § PWA Guardian.
**Verify:** DevTools offline mode → app renders in Fredoka (if self-hosted), or docs name the exception.
**Rule violated:** `CLAUDE.md` § Tech Stack & Zero-Cost Constraints (no CDN / fully offline)

### [POLISH] css/styles.css — dead `.sylly-toggle-on` rule

**Where:** `css/styles.css` line ~70 — `.sylly-toggle-on`
**What:** The deprecated `sylly-toggle-on` class has zero usages in `index.html` or any JS file (verified June 2026) but its CSS rule still exists.
**Why it matters:** Dead code invites accidental reuse of a deprecated pattern.
**Fix:** Delete the `.sylly-toggle-on` rule block (keep `.sylly-toggle-off` — it is a live legacy alias of `.game-toggle-off`).
**Verify:** `Select-String sylly-toggle-on` returns no hits in css/, js/, or index.html.
**Rule violated:** `phase-audit.md` Protocol A §2 (deprecated class)

## [DOC] items

### [DOC] index.html — game section header comments stale across ~9 sections

**Where:** `index.html` — the `<!-- ════ ... ════ -->` section header comment blocks
**What:** Scripted diff of header-claimed IDs vs actual markup (13 June 2026) found: all 8 per-game `[abbr]-help-tip-overlay`s (Phase 21a), both contextual tip overlays (`lttp-tip-overlay`, `bld-tip-overlay`), `nat-new-expedition-overlay`, `dyb-slick-picker-overlay`, `ss-dossier-overlay`, `ss-inning-transition`, `ss-endgame-splash`, `lttp-smalltalk-overlay`, `mp-host-prelobby-overlay`, and `screen-mp-roster` are present in the markup but claimed by no header. The LTTP header additionally states "screen-lttp-smalltalk removed Phase 21a" while that section still exists (see the separate orphaned-markup POLISH entry).
**Why it matters:** The headers are the in-file navigation map for a 6000+ line single-page file; stale lists send future sessions to `code-map.md` distrust or wrong conclusions.
**Fix:** Update each header's Screens/Overlays lists to match reality via a Node script (index.html bulk-edit rule). Pair with the `screen-lttp-smalltalk` deletion so the LTTP header note becomes true.
**Verify:** Re-run the header-claims diff script → zero unclaimed screens/overlays.
**Rule violated:** `logic-engine.md` § Checklist (section header comment block); Audit Principle 3

### [DOC] engine-multiplayer.js — `multiplayerOnly` config field is never read by any code

**Where:** `js/engine-multiplayer.js` — `MP_GAME_CONFIGS.*.multiplayerOnly`
**What:** Every config defines `multiplayerOnly`, and `game-identities.md` documents it as if it gates behaviour, but no code reads the field — MDLM-only routing is actually enforced by `supportedModes: ['mdlm']`.
**Why it matters:** A future game could set `multiplayerOnly: true` with a wider `supportedModes` list and expect a gate that doesn't exist.
**Fix:** Either remove the field (and the `multiplayerOnly: true` mentions in game-identities multiplayer sections become prose), or keep it and add a one-line "informational only — enforcement is `supportedModes`" note to `logic-engine.md` § Multiplayer Sync Module.
**Verify:** Grep all JS for `multiplayerOnly` consumption matches the chosen resolution.
**Rule violated:** Audit Principle 3 (reality wins)

**Where:** `.claude/rules/game-identities.md` § Game 11 Bailed (Overlay Types) vs `index.html` / `js/games/bld.js`
**What:** game-identities lists a `bld-new-night-overlay` ("New Night Out?" play-again confirmation). No such element exists. The shipped play-again flow (`#btn-bld-go-again`) opens `bld-second-chances-overlay` with a dynamic confirm label ("Restart in Lobby 🔄" host / "Leave Session" client / "Second Chances 💬" single) — the same overlay also serves the patience-exhausted Flake-win confirm.

**Verify:** game-identities BLD overlay table matches the `bld-*-overlay` IDs actually present in `index.html` (8 overlays).
**Rule violated:** Audit Principle 3 (reality wins)

### [DOC] SS — no Secret Mode expansion hook function exists

**Where:** `js/games/secret-signals.js` — no `ssApplyExpansionOverrides()` (was listed in `code-map.md` in error; removed in audit Phase 2)
**What:** The new-game checklist requires an `applyExpansionOverrides()` read at every plugin's settings-apply point ("retrofit existing games during Secret Mode build"), but SS has no such function. Whether SS handles expansion overrides another way, or deliberately skips Secret Mode support, is undocumented.
**Why it matters:** If SS is launchable from the Secret Mode terminal, host settings/word pools may silently ignore expansion overrides.
**Fix:** Phase 3 SS audit (Check G): trace how SS interacts with `SM_TERMINAL_CONFIG` / `secretWords`; either wire the hook or document the deliberate skip in game-identities + impl notes. Escalate to [BUG] if SS is selectable in the terminal but ignores overrides.
**Verify:** Either `ssApplyExpansionOverrides()` exists and is called at settings-apply, or the skip is documented.
**Rule violated:** `logic-engine.md` § Checklist: Adding a New Game (expansion hook)

### [DOC] DYB — Sylly Mode documented as "Chaos Mode"/Slick-only but shipped as "Devil's Luck" with 4+ die types

**Where:** `.claude/rules/game-identities.md` § Game 10 Dicey Bluffs vs `index.html` (DYB settings + how-to overlays)
**What:** `game-identities.md` names DYB's Sylly Mode "Chaos Mode" with only Slick dice; the shipped UI names it "Devil's Luck" and describes Loaded (count double), Phantom (hidden face), Slick (owner-assigned face), and Cracked (count zero) dice.
